name: Typefully
tagline: Writing, scheduling, and analytics for X/LinkedIn threads and posts

pricing.notes: Official pricing URL checked; public 2026 references list Creator around $12.50/month annual-effective, with monthly pricing varying by plan.
pricing.freeTier: The free plan allows 15 posts a month on one social set.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 1 social set, 1 user and 10 published posts/month.

tiers.name: Creator
tiers.limits: 1 user and unlimited scheduling; the current numeric social-set cap could not be independently extracted.
tiers.notes: Main live pricing page presents annual billing; the $12.50/month annual-equivalent amount is stated on current first-party Typefully comparison pages.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Team collaboration; social-set allowance varies by plan, but the current numeric price and cap were not recoverable from the client-rendered live widget.
tiers.notes: Official help says teammates may join without buying separate personal subscriptions.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 social set, 1 user and 10 posts per month.
pricing.billingTerms: Creator shown with annual billing on the live page; official billing help supports monthly/yearly switching generally; 14-day paid trial; Business amount not independently recoverable
pricing.hiddenCosts: Optional Extra AI Usage is metered, billed separately and may use a different billing cycle; current rates are not public. A spending cap is available, and usage charges are non-refundable.

verdictSummary: For personal thread drafting and scheduling, the core loop is vibecodable; the caveat is social API access, analytics, and platform-policy upkeep.
coreLoopDIY: Create a text editor for threads, preview character counts, store drafts, schedule via API, and track simple analytics.
whatYouLose: posting without paying X for API access
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because the editor reduces friction and posting works without API babysitting.

priorArt.name: Postiz
priorArt.desc: Open-source social scheduling prior art; can be adapted for thread workflows.

alternatives.name: BrightBean Studio
alternatives.desc: Draft and schedule threads for X and LinkedIn with analytics; the editor is less lovingly text-obsessed.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or clone the repository and deploy with Docker Compose or a supported PaaS.
facts.engines: No model is bundled; its REST API and MCP server connect external agents such as Claude Desktop/Code, Cursor or custom clients.
facts.dataFormat: Hosted data lives in BrightBean's cloud; self-hosted data uses PostgreSQL 16+ with media on local disk or S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Its general social composer is less polished for thread drafting, per-post previews and creator analytics than Typefully's text-first editor.
facts.setupBlocker: Connecting social networks requires first-party platform developer/OAuth credentials; self-hosting also requires Docker or a PaaS.

alternatives.name: Buffer Free
alternatives.desc: X threads and LinkedIn posts with ten queued items per channel; eight lifetime channel connections is the fine print.

facts.install: Hosted signup, with optional desktop browser extension and mobile apps.
facts.engines: Buffer AI Assistant is included, but Buffer's public product documentation does not identify its underlying model provider.
facts.dataFormat: Posts, media, ideas, connected-account metadata and analytics are stored in Buffer's cloud.
facts.gapVsPaid: Buffer Free limits each channel to ten queued items and lacks Typefully's deeper thread-writing and creator-analytics workflow.

alternatives.name: Fedica Free
alternatives.desc: Text-led cross-posting with ten live scheduled items; analytics are not Typefully-deep.

facts.install: Hosted signup and OAuth connection to each social account.
facts.dataFormat: Connected profiles, drafts, scheduled posts, media and analytics live in Fedica's cloud.
facts.gapVsPaid: Fedica's ten-item live queue and general analytics are a clear downgrade from Typefully's focused thread editor and performance feedback.

alternatives.name: Postiz
alternatives.desc: Threads, drafts, schedules and analytics across far more networks; operating it is the unlisted feature.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker Compose for self-hosting.
facts.engines: Optional AI/media features connect to OpenAI, ElevenLabs, fal.ai, Tavily, KieAI and Transloadit.
facts.dataFormat: PostgreSQL holds application data; Redis and Temporal support jobs; media is stored locally or in Cloudflare R2/S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Postiz is a general scheduler with a less refined thread-writing experience, and self-hosting replaces Typefully's managed simplicity.
facts.setupBlocker: Hosted use is straightforward; self-hosting requires Docker, social OAuth apps, and a PostgreSQL, Redis and Temporal stack.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Typefully Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free tier is real, but useful scheduling capacity and analytics are too restricted to replace the paid product.

notes: The composer and queue are easy. The catch is X's API pricing; the write tier costs more than Typefully does. That's the moat: not code, a paywall.
prompt:
Build me a tweet composer and scheduler like Typefully. Requirements:

- A local web app: compose posts and threads with live character count per
  post, split threads with "---", drag to reorder, image attachments, and a
  clean distraction-free writing view with drafts autosaved to SQLite.
- A queue: pick a time or "next free slot" (slots defined in a config file,
  e.g. weekdays 9:00 and 16:00). Calendar-style queue view grouped by day.
- Publishing via the X API v2 (keys in .env) · with an honest README section:
  the free API tier is read-only; posting needs the paid tier, which costs
  more than Typefully. Include a fallback "copy thread to clipboard" button
  and a browser-notification reminder at slot time so the tool stays useful
  without paying X anything.
- A cron-style loop in the same process publishes due queue items and marks
  results (posted / failed with error).
- Single Node process, no accounts, runs on localhost or a VPS.
